solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Equipment that can always let you down

definitions.text: Equipment that can always let you down

parts.words: Equipment that can always let you down
parts.note: a pun on 'let you down': not disappoint, but lower you gently to the ground from an aircraft

explanation.surface: A grumble about unreliable gear that always fails its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let you down' reads as a complaint, but the equipment does its job by lowering you safely from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Skydivers use this canopy device to descend slowly from an aircraft to the ground.

clue.text: Self-importance of parent banking millions

indicators.note: to bank something is to hold it safe, so the word for a parent here holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: pop is an informal word for a father
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A wealthy parent made pompous by the millions in their account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banking' looks like finance but signals POP wrapping round M.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy ceremony and swagger convey an inflated sense of one's own grandeur.

clue.text: Again let free

definitions.meaning: to let a property once more, split as re- plus lease

explanation.walkthrough: Split as RE-LEASE it means to rent out again; as one word it means to set loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Renting out a second time is leasing anew, and liberating a captive means setting it loose.

clue.text: Company on small Greek island

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A firm setting up on a little island in the Aegean.
explanation.definitionFit: Kos, also spelt Cos, is a Dodecanese isle in the Aegean Sea.

clue.text: Cheeky at university — shame

parts.note: UP means in residence at a university, as in 'up at Oxford'
'what a shame' means 'what a pity'

explanation.surface: A student's insolence at college is a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you are 'up' at university while studying there.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone impertinent who acts above their station.

clue.text: Pen that is put in envelope

definitions.meaning: a fenced area for keeping animals
an item inserted along with a letter in the same packet

explanation.definitionFit: A sheepfold is a fenced-off area, and an extra document sent with a letter is also called this.

clue.text: Greek character died in wet earth

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A figure from Greece perishing in boggy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Soil soaked with water becomes sticky mire.

clue.text: To chew noisily gets one thrown out of German city

indicators.note: something thrown out of a place is expelled from it, so the letter for one leaves the city's name

parts.note: Munich is the capital of Bavaria in Germany
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone eating loudly is ejected from a Bavarian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Crunching food audibly with steady jaw action is what this verb describes.

clue.text: After entrance, fail to make final desperate effort

indicators.note: the word for fail comes after the word for entrance in the answer

parts.note: a door is the way in to a room or building
an engine or a plan that fails is said to die

explanation.surface: Having got in, someone falls short of a last all-out attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a last-ditch all-out attempt where success or ruin are the only outcomes.

clue.text: Weakling gets full benefit of operation

parts.note: to milk a situation is to exploit it fully

explanation.surface: A feeble patient making the most of surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A timid, spineless person, especially a man, is called this old-fashioned insult.

clue.text: Direct the steering, then leave river

parts.note: to con a ship is to direct its course from the bridge
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Instructions to steer a vessel and then depart from a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is a nautical verb for directing a ship's helmsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A great African waterway that flows into the Atlantic bears this name.

clue.text: Turning to broadsheet, like an old tiger

indicators.note: turning the letters means twisting them about into a new order

explanation.surface: Switching to a serious newspaper, as a grizzled old beast might.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct prehistoric cat Smilodon had long curved fangs, giving it this descriptive name.

clue.text: Withdrew and negotiated again

definitions.meaning: dealt with or bargained a second time, split as re- plus treated

explanation.walkthrough: To treat is to negotiate, so RE-TREATED means negotiated again.
explanation.definitionFit: An army that fell back has withdrawn, and parties who bargained once more have dealt anew.

clue.text: Detective left in the US in exchange

indicators.note: letters in exchange swap places with one another, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sleuth left behind in America as part of a swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who investigates crimes and tracks down clues is a sleuth in this informal sense.

clue.text: Son nearly cut a lady from Italy

indicators.note: nearly means not quite the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: to cut someone is to ignore them deliberately

explanation.surface: A son almost snubbed an Italian woman.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Italian title for a married woman, equivalent to Mrs or madam.

clue.text: Warp belt's fastening

definitions.meaning: to bend or crumple out of shape
the clasp at the end of a belt

explanation.definitionFit: Metal that bends under strain does this, and the clasp of a strap carries the same name.

clue.text: Fortification on strike: no entry!

parts.note: a keep is the strongest tower of a castle
workers on strike are said to be out

explanation.surface: Pickets at a castle shouting that nobody may come in.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign warning trespassers away tells them they are not allowed in.

clue.text: Severe reprimand for firework

definitions.meaning: in British slang, getting a ... means a stern telling-off
a pyrotechnic that shoots up into the sky

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get a rocket' is British slang for being harshly told off.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh dressing-down in British slang shares its name with a skyward-shooting pyrotechnic.

clue.text: Sick, far gone, ended in paradise

indicators.note: sick here means unwell or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An ill person, far gone, died and went to heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the idyllic home of Adam and Eve is the original earthly bliss.

clue.text: Precarious run: one shown on satellite TV

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
I is the Roman numeral for one
Sky is a British satellite television broadcaster

explanation.surface: A dangerous run by someone appearing on a satellite channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a UK satellite TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hazardous or uncertain carries danger, so it is perilous.

clue.text: Lecherous look from king when speaking

indicators.note: speaking means said aloud, so the king's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: A monarch's lewd glance while giving a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A sly, lustful sideways stare at someone is what this word means.

clue.text: Start working with group

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: Beginning to work alongside a team.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of something, such as an illness or winter, is its commencement.

clue.text: Such a speech is a tonic

definitions.meaning: the main address that sets the theme of a conference
in music, the tonic is the first note of a scale, also called this

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tonic' looks like a pick-me-up but is the musical home note of a key.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal address at a conference shares a name with the first degree of a musical scale.

clue.text: That there is Yvonne, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters of the name are taken: first, third, fifth

explanation.surface: Pointing out a woman called Yvonne who behaves strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic or dialect word for something over there, at a distance, as in that hill yonder.

clue.text: A state in America, none in particular

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York state

explanation.surface: An American state that is nothing special.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'whichever one' means no specific choice is intended.

clue.text: One creating explosion when roster observed to be the wrong way round

indicators.text: to be the wrong way round
indicators.note: the wrong way round means read backwards from the last letter

parts.note: a rota is a roster of duties
noted means observed or noticed

explanation.surface: A blast happens when someone sees a duty list was back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be the wrong way round' reverses ROTANOTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that sets off a bomb's charge is what triggers the blast.
